introduction.definition: An effluent treatment plant (ETP) cleans industrial wastewater before discharge or reuse. Screening removes coarse solids, equalisation evens out flow and strength, neutralisation corrects pH, an activated-sludge aeration tank lets bacteria consume dissolved organic matter, and a secondary clarifier settles the biomass; most is returned (RAS) and the excess is wasted (WAS).
applications: Industrial effluents from food, chemical, textile, refinery and paper plants
key_points: RAS keeps biomass; WAS removes growth

pressure.title: Pollution load falls along the train
pressure.description: Screening removes rags and grit; equalisation evens out flow and strength; neutralisation brings pH into the ≈ 6–9 range the bacteria tolerate. In the aeration tank bacteria oxidise dissolved organic matter (BOD/COD) using oxygen from the diffusers (DO ≈ 1.5–2 mg/L), growing into flocs. The clarifier settles the flocs: most are returned (RAS) to keep the biomass (MLSS ≈ 2,000–4,000 mg/L), the growth is wasted (WAS), and clear treated effluent leaves over the weir — typically > 90 % BOD removal. Discharge limits are set by the local regulator.

foundation: Reinforced-concrete tank on prepared ground; watertightness test before backfill; allow for buoyancy when empty (groundwater).
alignment: Weirs and launders levelled to a few millimetres so overflow is even; drive/bridge centred and level.
piping: Inlet arranged to spread flow without short-circuiting; sludge lines with flushing points; overflow and drain to a safe place.
commissioning: Fill with clean water, check for leaks; run mechanisms empty and with water; start chemical dosing and tune by jar tests.

periodic.task: Clean screens; check diffusers and blower.

overhaul.task: Drain aeration tank; replace diffuser membranes.

lubrication: Motor and drive bearings greased / oiled to maker schedule; gearbox oil changed by hours or oil analysis.

causes: Filamentous bacteria (low DO, low F/M, nutrients)

safety: H₂S and confined spaces; biological hazards — hygiene; chemicals.

script.narration: This module introduces the Effluent Treatment Plant.
An effluent treatment plant (ETP) cleans industrial wastewater before discharge or reuse.

Screening removes coarse solids, equalisation evens out flow and strength, neutralisation corrects pH, an activated-sludge aeration tank lets bacteria consume dissolved organic matter, and a secondary clarifier settles the biomass; most is returned (RAS) and the excess is wasted (WAS).
Typical applications include industrial effluents from food, chemical, textile, refinery and paper plants; combined industrial/sanitary wastewater at sites.

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Mixer Propeller (keeps solids suspended), Equalisation Transfer Pump (steady feed), Equalisation Transfer Pump (steady feed) — Shaft & Coupling (turning), Neutralisation Tank: Agitator Shaft & Impellers.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.

video_tutorials.title: Effluent Treatment Plant — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Effluent Treatment Plant.
Check DO, pH, MLSS, sludge blanket and effluent quality.
Clean screens; check diffusers and blower.
Drain aeration tank; replace diffuser membranes.
Watch for sludge bulking: poor settling, turbid effluent. Common cause: filamentous bacteria (low DO, low F/M, nutrients).
Watch for toxic shock: DO rises, treatment stops. Common cause: toxic discharge.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
